page: Amazon Web Services m7i.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and fourth-generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (model 8488C) operating at 3.2 GHz. The system provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical execution cores via multithreading. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 system memory running at 5 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The instance does not feature local storage disks, relying instead on network-attached block storage, and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-threaded performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2025.0 and gzip compression throughput reaching 32.15 GB/sec. Text processing workloads also place in the upper quartile. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics like stress-ng multi-core and Clang software compilation fall in lower relative tiers due to the 4-thread execution cap. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 25.82 GB/sec, while write operations reach 27.32 GB/sec. The inclusion of Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets enables viable lightweight inference execution, recording 602.69 tokens/sec for prompt evaluation on a 135M parameter language model.

The m7i.xlarge offers balanced resource allocation for standard enterprise environments where high thread density or dedicated local NVMe throughput is not required. Because storage and enhanced networking rely on external fabrics, architectures must account for baseline network thresholds. The instance is suited for general web serving, application middleware, containerized services, microservices, and modest background data processing.

It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, accompanied by 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz. The instance configuration includes no bundled local storage, directing I/O to network-attached storage options, and maintains a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark profiles indicate strong single-core performance, reflected in single-threaded compression and text processing tests, while multi-core metrics remain moderate.
